samples.summary: The per-run surface pin does not look at a drag's `to` target, so `to.reader` is a cross-surface read the guard never sees
samples.evidence: `checkSurfaceScope` builds its `cited` list from only three places — `action.reader` (read/wait), `action.target.reader` and `action.expect.read` (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187). The new `drag` action introduces a FOURTH place a reader name can hide: `action.to.reader` (validated only for namespace prefix by `assertSafeActionPlan`, scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:163, and accepted verbatim by the zod schema at hunt-ui-tool.mjs:565). So a run assigned `slides` can submit `{type:"drag", target:{reader:"slides.elementCenter",args:["badge"]}, to:{reader:"sheet.cellCenter",args:["A1"]}}` and the surface pin returns null — the exact hole the function's own doc comment (lines 176-180) says the `target.reader` case exists to close. `readValue` in the runner then reads that reader through the bridge with no scope check (packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:214). Fix belongs on the new code: add `action?.to?.reader` to `cited`.

samples.summary: `isMutation` does not know about `drag`, so a drag between two clicks of the same control is recorded as a round trip that never happened
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:160-164 classifies mutations as `type`, `key`, or a `click` with a control; `drag` is absent, yet a drag mutates the slide (it is the whole point of the change). Two consequences in the same loop: (a) at line 254-265 a non-click action only resets `lastControl`/`lastMutationControl` when `isMutation(action)` is true, so `click Bold` → `drag element` → `click Bold` still sets `seen.roundTripped = true` at line 275 — precisely the false claim the comment at 255-259 says the reset exists to prevent; (b) at line 245-252 a pending `mutationPendingRead` is not cleared by an intervening drag, so a later read is credited as "effect observed before anything else touched the document" (line 247) when a drag did touch it. Both corrupt the persisted coverage memory that drives the next run's brief.

verdict.reason: The code gap is present as described (checkSurfaceScope omits action.to.reader at scripts/agent/hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187 while drag's `to` accepts a reader, hunt-ui-tool.mjs:565), but the harm it claims — a cross-surface read the guard never sees — is unreachable because a second, independent guard blocks it. Every surface reader in the page bridge routes through requireSheet/requireDoc/requireSlides (bridge.ts:171-190; e.g. sheet.cellCenter at bridge.ts:649-651, slides.elementCenter at bridge.ts:610-612), which refuse when that surface's handle is absent, and unknown names are refused at bridge.ts:728-730. Handles are mutually exclusive: only the doc branch calls setDoc, only the slides branch setSlides, only the sheet branch setSheet (page.tsx:397-479), and no other file in packages/frontend/src sets them. The mounted surface can never differ from the run's assigned surface: goto's surface is a single-member zod enum (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:559) and is re-checked by the pin (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:198-200), the runner navigates only on goto (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:282), and the page starts blank with no bridge installed until then (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:353-369, 199-206). Consequently a slides run submitting to:{reader:"sheet.cellCenter"} gets a bridge refusal, not another surface's data; the value-leaking message at hunt-ui-runner.mjs:219 is never reached because readValue throws first. The residual issue is a lower-quality error instead of a policy refusal (a cheap one-line hardening), not a reachable guard bypass, so it does not meet the blast-radius bar for major/blocking.

verdict.reason: Present and reachable as described. `isMutation` (scripts/agent/hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:160-164) classifies only `type`, `key`, and named `click` as mutating; `drag` is absent. `drag` is a real action in this tree — added to the closed vocabulary at hunt-ui-probe.mjs:44 (the baseline .trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:44 has no `drag`), validated at hunt-ui-probe.mjs:154-164, exposed at hunt-ui-tool.mjs:564-565, executed via performDrag at packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:296-307, and documented as mutating the slide in charters-ui/slide-author.md:60-81. Every action including drag is journaled at hunt-ui-tool.mjs:439-447 and that journal is fed to coverageFromJournal and merged into persisted memory at hunt-ui.mjs:1401-1406. Consequence (a): a drag takes the `action.type !== "click"` branch at hunt-ui-coverage.mjs:254-265, isMutation is false, so lastControl/lastMutationControl survive, and `click Bold` → `drag` → `click Bold` sets roundTripped at line 275 — the precise false claim the comment at 255-259 says the reset prevents (it also lets pairs record a false adjacency at 280-282). Consequence (b): mutationPendingRead is neither consumed nor cleared by a drag at 245-252, so a later read is falsely credited at line 247. No guard filters drags out beforehand — the only early continue is the failed-click filter at line 210 — and hunt-ui-coverage.test.mjs has no drag coverage. This is a new vocabulary member with an unupdated consumer in an untouched module, squarely in the blast-radius lane, and it corrupts persisted coverage that drives the next run's brief: major.

verdict.reason: Code is present as described. `target(action)` (scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:370-377) reads only `action?.target` (`.name` or `.reader`), and `uiDefectKey` composes `personaId|type|on|read|op|ground` at line 398 (and `...|oracles:...` at 407) with no component derived from `action.to`. The new `drag` action genuinely has a destination of identical shape (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:565; hunt-ui-probe.mjs:162-163 validates both ends), and journal entries store the whole action object, so `to` is available and simply unused. This is blast-radius, not diff-internal logic: the baseline lacks `drag` entirely (.trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-ui-probe.mjs:44) while `.trusted/scripts/agent/hunt-ui.mjs:370-408` is identical to the current `uiDefectKey`, i.e. a new action type with a new essential field whose untouched downstream consumer was not updated. Reachable: keyOf at hunt-ui.mjs:1462 feeds dedupeCandidates at 1494, which keeps only the first candidate per key, so the second drag defect is excluded from verification. The reviewer's specific `se`-handle example is inaccurate (a handle drag's origin reader is `slides.handleCenter`, distinct from `slides.elementCenter` — charters-ui/slide-author.md:66-67), but valid collisions exist (same reader origin to two different destinations; `target()` also drops reader args, so different elements collide too), so the central claim stands. The collapse logging at hunt-ui.mjs:1480-1493 records the collapse but still drops the candidate, so it does not guard the loss.
